citation.title: Topology optimization for heat transfer problems: towards a finite element based neural network approach
citation.venue: M.Sc. thesis in Computational Science and Engineering, Politecnico di Milano (supervisors: Prof. Nicola Parolini, Prof. Marco Verani; Academic Year 2019-2020)
citation.version_coded: Version of record (the only version), 100-page PDF obtained from the Politecnico di Milano institutional thesis repository (PoliTesi), https://www.politesi.polimi.it/handle/10589/165067 (retrieve link https://www.politesi.polimi.it/retrieve/a81cb05d-bf3f-616b-e053-1605fe0a889a/thesis_Elisabetta_Chimisso.pdf); title page, abstract, table of contents and the Conclusions chapter (Ch. 6) were read in full to confirm document type and topic before stopping per the FT-TYPE exclusion rule

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded). Headline: the thesis proposes a per-problem 'ANN-FE' hybrid method for topology optimization of heat-transfer (cooling-system) problems, in which a finite element method solves the governing PDE while an artificial neural network parameterizes the material-distribution field directly (optimization is performed over the ANN's own weights/biases rather than over per-element FEM design variables); the Conclusions chapter (Ch. 6) also proposes a multigrid-inspired ('V-cycle') scheme for training the ANN hierarchically, layer-group by layer-group, and states this is shown to reduce computational cost relative to training the full network directly.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded at full text). Not assessed in detail; the Conclusions chapter states the V-cycle training scheme 'is proven to increase the performances of the optimization in terms of computational cost' without a number in the passage read.

notes: No author named Jun Wang (sole author: Elisabetta Chimisso; supervisors Nicola Parolini and Marco Verani are not authors).
